To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the provision of water storage hardware to shared toilet users is an effective way to increase toilet cleaning and improve toilet maintenance behaviour.

the use of behaviour change communications to promote the consistent use of water for toilet cleaning and maintenance is an effective approach to address water scarcity and improve the hygienic use and maintenance of shared toilets in low‐income areas of Dhaka, Bangladesh.

(1) water scarcity is an important constraint on toilet maintenance behaviours and (2) behaviour change interventions that address water scarcity may be effective at promoting toilet maintenance and hygiene practices among users of shared urban toilets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of low‐cost interventions that address the scarcity of water to improve the hygiene and health of shared toilet users.
how to improve toilet use in the context of scarce resources, and the implications of this for public health and development.
understanding the social and physical factors that influence toilet maintenance behaviours, and developing and testing interventions to improve them.

the use of a water storage device, in combination with a toilet behaviour change communication, was associated with a significant increase in the proportion of users who reported that they were able to flush the toilet.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the provision of water storage hardware and behaviour change communication (BCC) messages to improve toilet cleaning behaviour can be an effective strategy to reduce the spread of infectious diseases in urban slum settings.

we developed a behaviour change communication and low‐cost water management intervention that can improve toilet maintenance behaviours, and therefore the hygienic use and health impact of shared toilets.
the provision of toilets is necessary, but not sufficient to improve health.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of behaviour change communications should be based on a thorough understanding of the context and that the design of low‐cost hardware should be based on user needs.
behaviour change communications and water storage hardware are necessary to ensure that shared toilets are maintained and hygienically used.
water is a prerequisite for toilet function, maintenance, and hygiene.
